skill.name: ci-cd-and-automation
skill.description: Designs and improves CI/CD pipelines with quality gates, automated testing, secure secret handling, staged deployments, and rollback plans.
skill.summary: Build reliable CI/CD pipelines with automated checks, deployment controls, and rollback guidance.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings describe commands, secret placeholders, environment-file guidance, or warning text inside SKILL.md examples. They are false positives for direct malware behavior because the skill contains documentation and configuration templates, not executable code or unauthorized data access. No additional semantic security finding was identified.

remediation.issue: Workflow examples invoke third-party actions and deployment tools.
remediation.suggestion: Pin third-party actions and deployment dependencies to trusted commit SHAs, and review upgrades before merging.

remediation.issue: The rollback example interpolates a workflow input into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the version against an allowlisted format and pass it through a safely quoted environment variable before invoking the deployment tool.

remediation.issue: Database credentials appear in example connection strings.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the documented secret references, use ephemeral CI credentials, and prevent connection strings from appearing in logs or artifacts.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable checks and controlled releases to reduce broken builds and deployment risk. This skill provides practical pipeline, testing, rollout, secret, and rollback guidance.
actual_capabilities: Design CI pipelines with lint, type checking, tests, builds, security audits, and bundle checks.
Create GitHub Actions workflow templates for Node.js projects and database integration tests.
Recommend E2E testing, preview deployments, feature flags, staged rollouts, and rollback plans.
Explain CI secret separation, environment-file practices, and protected deployment credentials.
Suggest caching, parallel jobs, path filters, matrix builds, and test-suite optimization.
Define branch protection, required reviews, status checks, and controlled auto-merge policies.
limitations: It does not run pipelines, inspect repositories, or verify that example commands match a specific project.
It focuses on general GitHub Actions and Node.js examples rather than every CI provider or runtime.
It does not replace security review, secret rotation, dependency review, or deployment-platform documentation.
Generated workflows require project-specific testing, permissions review, input validation, and credential configuration.

use_cases.title: Set Up Project CI
use_cases.description: Create a pull request and main-branch pipeline with quality gates for linting, types, tests, builds, and dependency audits.

use_cases.title: Improve Release Safety
use_cases.description: Plan preview environments, feature flags, staged production rollouts, monitoring windows, and reliable rollback procedures.

use_cases.title: Speed Up Slow Builds
use_cases.description: Diagnose long CI runs and apply caching, parallel jobs, path filters, matrix testing, or targeted test optimization.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub Actions CI workflow for my Node.js project. Include install, lint, type checking, tests, build, and security audit steps. Ask for missing project details first.

prompt_templates.title: Add Database Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my CI workflow with a temporary PostgreSQL service and integration tests. Use protected CI secrets, avoid production credentials, and list the project-specific values I must configure.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safer Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release workflow using preview deployments, feature flags, staged rollout approval, monitoring, and rollback. Identify permission boundaries and secret-handling risks.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Slow Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CI timing summary and propose an implementation plan using caching, parallel jobs, path filters, matrix builds, and test optimization. Preserve required quality gates and explain tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: A Node.js team wants every pull request to pass standard quality checks before merge.
output_examples.output: A workflow plan with dependency installation, linting, type checking, unit tests with coverage, a production build, a high-severity dependency audit, and required status checks.

output_examples.input: An application needs database integration tests without exposing production credentials.
output: Start an isolated PostgreSQL service in the CI runner.
Use a dedicated CI secret for the test password.
Keep production credentials outside the CI environment.

output_examples.input: A pipeline takes more than ten minutes and repeats the same dependency work.
output_examples.output: An optimization sequence that enables dependency caching, splits independent checks into parallel jobs, filters jobs by changed paths, and measures each change against required gates.

best_practices: Keep lint, type, test, build, and security checks required before merge.
Use separate least-privilege CI credentials and store secrets in the platform secret manager.
Make deployments reversible with staged verification, monitoring, and a tested rollback path.
anti_patterns: Disabling tests or weakening required checks to make a pipeline pass.
Using production credentials in CI or committing real secrets to environment files.
Deploying directly to production without staging verification, monitoring, or rollback.

faq.question: What projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It primarily provides GitHub Actions and Node.js examples, but the practices apply to most CI/CD platforms and runtimes.

faq.question: Does this skill execute my pipeline?
faq.answer: No. It produces planning and configuration guidance. You must review, adapt, and run the workflow in your own repository.

faq.question: How should CI credentials be managed?
faq.answer: Use dedicated, least-privilege test credentials stored in a secret manager. Keep production credentials out of CI jobs.

faq.question: When should I use feature flags?
faq.answer: Use them when deployment and release timing must be separated, especially for risky changes or gradual user rollouts.

faq.question: How can I reduce CI duration?
faq.answer: Start with dependency caching and parallel jobs. Then use path filters, matrix testing, and targeted test-suite improvements.

faq.question: What should every deployment rollback plan include?
faq.answer: Define a known previous version, an authorized trigger, input validation, monitoring after rollback, and a tested recovery procedure.
